attributes.body_ja:
「ず」は「ぬ」や「ない」と同（おな）じように動詞（どうし）を否定形（ひていけい）に変（か）える、古典（こてん）の助動詞（じょどうし）です。（古典（こてん）の助動詞（じょどうし）なので、現代（げんだい）の基本的（きほんてき）な助動詞（じょどうし）１８（じゅうはっ）種類（しゅるい）の中（なか）には入（はい）っていません。）「ずに」は、この助動詞（じょどうし）「ず」に格助詞（かくじょし）の「に」を付（つ）けた形（かたち）です。二（ふた）つを合（あ）わせると、「ないで」と同（おな）じ意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）します。

「ずに」は、「ない」と同（おな）じように、否定（ひてい）したい動詞（どうし）の未然形（みぜんけい）に付（つ）けて使（つか）われます。

「ずに」は「ないで」よりもフォーマルな表現（ひょうげん）です。また、現代（げんだい）では特（とく）に「ずに済（す）む」のような決（き）まった表現（ひょうげん）の中（なか）で使（つか）われています。（「ずに済（す）む」は、別（べつ）のレッスンで学（まな）びます）。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

「ず」がスル動詞（どうし）に付（つ）くときは、「しずに」ではなく、「せずに」という形（かたち）になります。「せ」も「し」も「する」の未然形（みぜんけい）ではありますが、「し」（東日本（ひがしにほん）でよく使（つか）われる）は「ない」と合（あ）わせるときに使（つか）われます。
attributes.body:
Although it is not considered to be one of the primary 18 auxiliary verbs that are used in modern Japanese, ず is a classical auxiliary verb that has the same role as ぬ, and ない. This role is negating the verb that it is attached to. ずに is simply the addition of the case marking particle に to ず. Together, they mean 'without doing', in a similar way to ないで.

To use ずに, attach it to the indeterminate form of the verb that you wish to express as 'without doing (A)'. This is the same form used with ない.

ずに is quite a bit more formal than ないで, but still frequently used in modern Japanese. Especially as part of set phrases, like ずにすむ (which we will learn about in another lesson).

Caution

When used with a する verb, する will become せずに, not しずに. Both せ and し are indeterminate forms of する. し, the more common form that is used in east Japan appears with ない.

attributes.source: [AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.description: Can you distinguish ないで / なくて / ずに？
Doing something without doing something else

attributes.body: ないで and ずに both express the idea of 'without doing (A)' and are used in similar ways. For example, 朝ご飯を食べないで学校に行った and 朝ご飯を食べずに学校に行った both mean 'I went to school without eating breakfast.', but ずに has a slightly more formal or literary tone, while ないで is more conversational. Unlike ないで, ずに cannot be used as a negative request form to say 'Don't (A).'.

ずに has the core meaning of 'without doing', while ずにはいられない is an idiomatic form meaning 'I can't help but (A)'. Compare '宿題をせずに寝た' ('I went to bed without doing my homework'), which describes inaction, to '彼の話に笑わずにはいられなかった' ('I couldn't help but laugh at his story'), which expresses an uncontrollable response.

second_relatable.title: ずにはいられない
second_relatable.meaning: Cannot help doing something, Cannot resist doing something

attributes.body: ずに has the core meaning of 'without doing', and ずに済む is an idiomatic usage of meaning 'not having to do (A)' (literally, 'it works out without doing it'). Compare 宿題をせずに寝た ('I went to bed without doing my homework.'), which simply describes lack of action, to e.g. 新しいスマホを買わずに済んだ ('It worked out so that I didn't have to buy a new smartphone.').

second_relatable.title: ずに済む
second_relatable.meaning: Get by without doing something, To get away with

attributes.body: Both ずに and ことなく mean 'without doing (A)' and can often be used interchangeably. ずに is more common and used in both writing and conversation, e.g. '宿題をせずに寝た' ('I went to bed without doing my homework'). ことなく is more formal and tends to appear in writing, e.g. '彼は休むことなく働き続けた' ('He continued working without rest').
